what_its_for: Cyclophosphamide is a chemotherapy medicine used to treat several types of cancer, including breast cancer, leukemia, lymphoma, and others. It is also sometimes used to treat serious autoimmune diseases like lupus or certain kidney conditions. It works by slowing or stopping the growth of cancer cells in your body.
how_to_take: Take cyclophosphamide exactly as your doctor tells you. It comes as a tablet you swallow by mouth, or it may be given as an injection by a healthcare provider at a clinic or hospital. If you are taking the tablet at home, swallow it whole with a full glass of water. Do NOT crush, break, or chew the tablet. Take it in the morning if possible, and drink plenty of fluids (at least 6 to 8 glasses of water or other non-alcoholic beverages) throughout the day unless your doctor tells you otherwise. This helps protect your bladder. You may take it with or without food, but if it upsets your stomach, try taking it with food or milk.
dosing: Your dose will be carefully calculated by your doctor based on your body size, the condition being treated, and how well your kidneys and blood cells are working. Everyone's dose is different, so never share this medicine or take a dose prescribed for someone else. Your doctor may adjust your dose during treatment based on lab results and how your body responds. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions and the label on your prescription bottle.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, call your doctor or pharmacist right away for instructions. Do NOT take a double dose to make up for the one you missed. Because this is a powerful medicine, it is very important to follow a specific schedule, so your care team will tell you exactly what to do.
storage: Store cyclophosphamide tablets at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep them away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Do not store in the bathroom. Keep this medicine in its original container with the cap tightly closed. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Ask your pharmacist how to safely dispose of any leftover or expired medicine.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking this medicine, as it can increase the risk of side effects. Do not get any live vaccines (such as the live flu nasal spray or shingles vaccine) without talking to your doctor first, because cyclophosphamide weakens your immune system. Avoid contact with people who are sick or have infections. Avoid becoming pregnant or fathering a child while on this medicine, as it can harm an unborn baby. Use effective birth control during treatment and for a period of time after, as directed by your doctor. Women who are breastfeeding should not take this medicine. Avoid handling broken tablets with bare hands — if a tablet breaks, do not handle it without gloves.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you notice any of the following: blood in your urine or pain when urinating (signs of bladder irritation or bleeding), fever of 100.4°F (38°C) or higher (could be a sign of infection), unusual bruising or bleeding, extreme tiredness or weakness, shortness of breath or chest pain, yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice), severe nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea that you cannot control, mouth sores that make it hard to eat or drink, swelling in your legs or feet, or signs of a serious allergic reaction such as rash, hives, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing.
when_it_works: Cyclophosphamide starts working in your body right away, but you may not feel or see the results immediately. For cancer treatment, your doctor will monitor your response through regular blood tests and imaging scans. For autoimmune conditions, it may take several weeks to months before you notice improvement. It is important to keep all of your follow-up appointments so your doctor can check how well the medicine is working and watch for side effects.
special_populations: Children: Cyclophosphamide is used in children for certain cancers, but doses are carefully calculated based on body size and monitored closely by a specialist. Older adults: Elderly patients may be more sensitive to side effects, especially effects on blood cells and the bladder, so closer monitoring may be needed. Pregnancy: This medicine can cause serious harm to an unborn baby and should NOT be used during pregnancy. Use reliable birth control. Talk to your doctor before trying to get pregnant after finishing treatment. Breastfeeding: Do not breastfeed while taking this medicine, as it passes into breast milk and can harm a nursing infant. Kidney or liver problems: Your doctor may need to adjust your dose if you have kidney or liver disease, so always inform your doctor of any existing conditions.
